To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nearest neighbor search can improve the quality of pre-trained LMs, that it can be applied without additional training, and that it can be used for domain adaptation.
we introduce a new method for language modeling that is more effective than the current state-of-the-art and that it has implications for scaling up language models and adapting to new domains.

(1) nearest neighbor models are effective for language modeling; (2) nearest neighbor models can be combined with pre-trained LMs to improve performance; (3) nearest neighbor models scale well with training data, even when the training data is not used to train the pre-trained LM; and (4) nearest neighbor models allow for domain adaptation without re-training, which could be important for low-resource domains.

the following question: How can a neural language model be made more general? Our answer: by making it more specific.
